name: Quételet’s comparative social statistics
description: Quételet compared aggregate social and demographic observations using administrative statistics.

impact.note: Applied statistical comparison to social data for statisticians and officials, extending earlier political arithmetic; social statistics and later quantitative social science built on it.

date.basis: Dated publication, legal decision, institution or documented practice; not a global origin claim.

events.statement: In his 1835 social-physics book, Quételet analyzed French court statistics from 1826–1831.
events.scope: This documented community and episode; not a universal first.

evidence.supports: The history dates the book and identifies the period of the court records.
The contemporary review describes comparisons by place and demographic characteristics.
The history dates the book and identifies the period of the court records.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence gathered for this scoped capability, not global priority.

caveats: Court statistics capture recorded prosecutions and their institutional context, not all offenses; his predictions and ideas of social regularity are historical interpretations, not established social laws.

research.note: Initial source pass; independent review is outstanding. Independent review verified the book and French 1826–1831 court records in the MacTutor excerpt; the contemporary review PDF was inaccessible, so wider comparisons remain sourced. Independent review checked Aubusson de Cavarlay p. 156 on Quételet’s early use of the 1826–1829 Compte volumes; this supports the connection to the series, not personal use of the 1825 volume.

places.note: France identifies the court statistics’ geographic coverage; the cited passage does not establish the author’s location while writing.

links.statement: Quételet’s early crime-statistics work used volumes of the French Compte général, according to historian Aubusson de Cavarlay.

evidence.supports: Identifies the 1826–1829 Compte volumes used by Quételet.
